source.title: Prioritizing Image-Related Tokens Enhances Vision-Language Pre-Training
source.authors: Yangyi Chen; Hao Peng; Tong Zhang; Heng Ji

record.tranche_reason: The study fits a scaling function to downstream benchmark performance and tests prediction at a larger data scale in vision-language models. This is a conceptual test of downstream predictability, using different models and measures from the original language-model loss laws.
record.gate_note: The scaling analysis measures downstream benchmark performance, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy. The token-subset loss comparison in Figure 8 is also not a scaling-law test; it is recorded under fits_no_version. Main benchmark comparisons over training steps and claims cited from other papers are not rows for the versions here.
record.test_reason: In §3.5 the study fits a power law in training tokens to downstream benchmark performance of two LVLM types, trained with NTP and with PRIOR on 7M–70M tokens (8 models). It then measures relative prediction error at 100M tokens. That is a downstream-predictability result (V6) in a new setting: vision-language pre-training. Most of the paper is about its own method, but the NTP fits are a standard-training result. T3 fits better than T2 because the setting, not the method, is what is new. The extrapolation is only about 1.4x beyond the largest fitted run.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that PRIOR beats NTP by about 19% (H-LVLM) and 8% (U-LVLM) on average, trains more stably, and scales more predictably with higher αD. The predictability claim is relative to NTP and covers downstream benchmarks only, fitted on 7M–70M tokens. They also note, citing [15], that NTP loss does not track downstream performance in LVLMs.
record.recipe_differences: Fits a data-scaling function to downstream LVLM benchmark performance; does not reproduce the original studies' held-out language-model loss measurements or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ by training objective (PRIOR versus NTP) and are reported separately for H-LVLM and U-LVLM architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: PRIOR-trained H-LVLMs have lower average NTP loss than NTP-trained ones on both image-related and image-unrelated tokens. The gap is larger for image-related tokens and grows with the importance threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Token-level importance reweighting reduces LVLM loss on token subsets, and the reduction is larger for tokens with higher image relevance.

record.problems: Scaling results are presented in figures without numerical coefficient or prediction-error values in the text. The scaling target is downstream benchmark performance rather than held-out pretraining loss, and the evaluated data range is 7M to 70M training tokens with prediction at 100M tokens.

untested.parts: Prediction from pretraining loss; text-only LLMs; extrapolation over orders of magnitude (here only 70M→100M tokens); scaling in parameters or compute rather than tokens.
Held-out pretraining loss scaling is not measured.
Loss extrapolation is not tested. Only downstream performance is extrapolated, and over a small range.
The LVLM fits are on downstream performance, not loss, so loss-law form in other modalities is not tested.
Fit-method or setup dependence of loss exponents is not tested. The only variation is the training objective, and it affects downstream fits.

missing.what: Numeric relative prediction errors and αD values for NTP and PRIOR. These are shown only in figures, which the extracted text does not render.

record.verdict_notes: Every V6 row rests on figure-only results plus qualitative text. The extrapolation span (70M→100M tokens) is far short of 'orders of magnitude'. The cited statement that NTP loss does not reliably predict downstream LVLM performance comes from [15] and is not this study's result, so it is not a row. Fig. 1, Fig. 3 and Fig. 9 report benchmark scores over training steps, not scaling fits, and are rightly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pretraining loss scaling with parameter count, tokens, or compute is tested.
The study predicts downstream benchmark performance at a larger data scale, not held-out loss of larger language-model runs from smaller runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between model parameters and training tokens is tested.
No comparison of architecture details at fixed parameter count is reported.

Although the models are vision-language models, the scaling outcome is downstream benchmark performance rather than held-out pretraining loss; the claimed loss-law form in other modalities or regimes is therefore not tested.
Tests downstream benchmark predictability when varying training data for two LVLM architectures; does not test prediction from pretraining loss or downstream tasks for text-only LLMs.
Does not test how published loss-law exponents or compute-optimal allocations depend on parameter counting, training schedule, data, or fitting choices.

relationships.condition: PRIOR-trained H-LVLM and U-LVLM, token-count power law fitted on 7M–70M tokens, predicting 100M
relationships.reason: The authors report that PRIOR-trained models' downstream performance is predictable at 100M tokens (r2, r4). The values are figure only and the extrapolation is about 1.4x.
relationships.display_finding: Fitted power laws predicted downstream performance at 100M tokens after fitting 7M–70M tokens, an extrapolation of about 1.4×.

relationships.condition: Standard NTP-trained H-LVLM and U-LVLM, same fit and prediction target
relationships.reason: Downstream performance under standard NTP is stated to be significantly less predictable than under PRIOR (r1, r3). So predictability depends on the training objective.
relationships.display_finding: Downstream performance was significantly less predictable under standard NTP than under PRIOR, showing dependence on the training objective.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: PRIOR-trained H-LVLM and U-LVLM, for downstream benchmark performance predicted from the tested data range at 100M tokens
reader_labels.reason: The authors report significantly higher prediction accuracy for PRIOR than NTP in both architectures (r2, r4). They also report higher scaling coefficients for PRIOR (r6, r8).
